qualifying_findings.title: Aider repository configuration can execute shell commands
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVE Program record assigned by VulnCheck with repository source references
qualifying_findings.security_fact: Aider through 0.86.2 auto-loads a repository .aider.conf.yml without a trust prompt. A committed notifications-command or editor value reaches subprocess execution with shell=True after a model reply or editor use.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: aider-chat through 0.86.2; untrusted repository configuration to local coding-agent shell-execution boundary.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: No fixed release was named in the public CVE record. Do not open untrusted repositories with affected versions; review or remove .aider.conf.yml before use and run the agent with least privilege.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A repository is an untrusted input to a coding agent; configuration must not silently acquire authority to execute local commands.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad Aider catalog context; this repository retains the repository-configuration trust and command-execution boundary.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for the affected version, mechanism, and publication time. The CVE record says no fixed release; confirm maintainer remediation during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Check the maintainer issue and later release notes for a fixed version or trust-prompt behavior before operational guidance.

qualifying_findings.title: Malicious npm agent-skill collections disclosed
qualifying_findings.security_fact: GitHub marked published versions of npm packages agentic-awesome-skills and opencode-skills-collection as malware. The advisories state that a computer where either package was installed or run should be treated as fully compromised and that secrets and keys should be rotated from a different computer.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: 20 listed versions of each npm skill-collection package, including agentic-awesome-skills 18.9.0 through 19.13.0 listed versions and opencode-skills-collection 4.0.56 through 4.1.20 listed versions; installable agent-skill package supply chain.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Remove affected packages, investigate the host as compromised, and rotate stored secrets and keys from a separate trusted computer. No patched version is identified by either advisory.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent skills can carry execution, credential, and tool authority; package provenance and staged review are supply-chain controls rather than optional convenience checks.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad agent-skill and package catalog context; this repository retains the malware disclosure and agent-execution supply-chain implication.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for publication timing, malware classification, and response recommendation from GitHub-reviewed advisory records. The advisories do not describe payload behavior.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, retain the two advisories as distinct package incidents and avoid inferring payload capabilities not published by GitHub.

qualifying_findings.title: AWS Multi Model Server model artifact traversal and SSRF
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database records referencing an AWS security bulletin and NVD CVE records
qualifying_findings.security_fact: AWS Multi Model Server 1.1.11 and earlier permits arbitrary code execution through relative path traversal while extracting a crafted model archive, and SSRF through a crafted model download URL.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: AWS Multi Model Server 1.1.11 and earlier; model artifact extraction and model-download URL to runtime/filesystem and internal-network boundaries.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: The product is end of life and has no fixed version. Discontinue use and migrate to a supported model-serving solution.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model archives and model URLs are high-risk supply-chain inputs; an end-of-life serving runtime leaves both code-execution and internal-network exposure without a patch path.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad AWS and model-serving catalog context; this repository retains the model-artifact extraction, model-download SSRF, and unsupported-runtime security implications.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for the two mechanisms, affected version, no-fix state, and visible advisory publication time. Recheck the AWS bulletin during ingest for any deployment-specific guidance.
follow_up_actions: Treat the two CVEs as separate technical boundaries during synthesis while preserving their shared end-of-life migration response.

qualifying_findings.title: MLflow GenAI scorer endpoint SSRF
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Maintainer GitHub security advisory with fix commit and release reference
qualifying_findings.security_fact: On an unauthenticated MLflow server with optional trulens and trulens-providers-litellm installed, attacker-supplied third-party scorer JSON can instantiate an allowed-module class with unconstrained kwargs and cause the server to make an HTTP request to an attacker-chosen host.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mlflow >=3.12.0rc0 and <3.17.0 under the optional GenAI evaluation dependency configuration; unauthenticated scorer invoke/register/evaluate input to outbound LLM-client request boundary.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade to MLflow 3.17.0. Require authentication on tracking servers and restrict outbound network access as defense in depth.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Evaluation endpoints can turn attacker-controlled scorer configuration into privileged server-side model-provider or internal-network requests.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad MLflow and evaluation-tool context; this repository retains the unauthenticated GenAI-evaluation SSRF and egress-control boundary.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for timing, conditions, fixed version, and mechanism from the maintainer advisory.
follow_up_actions: Verify the release artifact and scope of affected optional dependencies during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: LangGraph persisted namespace collision crosses tenant boundaries
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Maintainer GitHub security advisory with fix commit and release references
qualifying_findings.security_fact: LangGraph Postgres and SQLite stores serialize namespace labels with a dot delimiter, making tuples such as (tenant, bob) collide with (tenant.bob). Several read, search, delete, listing, and batch paths did not reject dot-containing untrusted labels, enabling cross-namespace reads, overwrites, or deletes.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: langgraph-checkpoint-postgres before 3.1.3 and langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite before 3.1.2 when tenants rely on namespaces and untrusted input reaches those methods; InMemoryStore is not affected.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade the Postgres store to 3.1.3 or SQLite store to 3.1.2 together with langgraph-checkpoint 4.3.0; reject empty, non-string, and dot-containing labels across all direct and batch operations.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent memory and state stores frequently use namespaces as authorization boundaries; lossy serialization can convert user input into cross-tenant data access or instruction-state tampering.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad LangGraph and LangSmith context; this repository retains tenant-state isolation and namespace-validation implications.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for scope, non-affected store, affected versions, and remediation from the maintainer advisory.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, relate this to local agent-memory isolation guidance without duplicating upstream LangGraph product analysis.

qualifying_findings.title: FastMCP authorization and OAuth issuer-binding defects
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Maintainer-accepted GitHub security advisories with fixed releases
qualifying_findings.security_fact: FastMCP direct lookups authorized an original component but could return a transformed component without rechecking its policy, allowing a low-privilege caller to invoke protected tools or retrieve protected resources, templates, or prompts. Separately, FastMCP M2M OAuth wrappers lacked authorization-server issuer binding, allowing an untrusted or compromised MCP server to redirect client credentials or signed assertions to an attacker-advertised authorization server.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Authorization flaw: fastmcp and fastmcp-slim 3.0.0–3.4.9 and 4.0.0–4.1.1 with component authorization/transforms. Issuer-binding flaw: fastmcp and fastmcp-slim 4.0.0a1–4.1.1; MCP client credential to discovered authorization-server boundary.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade 3.x to 3.4.10 and 4.x to 4.1.2. For issuer binding, explicitly configure issuer after upgrading and rotate reusable client credentials that may have been exposed; upgrade alone leaves the compatibility omission available with a warning.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP policy must apply to the final invoked capability, and OAuth credentials must be bound to the authorization server that owns them rather than trusting server-discovered metadata.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad FastMCP and MCP catalog context; this repository retains final-capability authorization and issuer-bound credential controls.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for each mechanism, affected release line, and remediation. The advisories are distinct and share the 4.1.2 release; do not merge their control boundaries during synthesis.
follow_up_actions: Verify configuration migration for issuer and whether affected deployments cache reusable credentials before publishing operating guidance.

qualifying_findings.title: vLLM multimodal request controls permit remote service crashes
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Maintainer GitHub security advisories with fix commits and release reference
qualifying_findings.security_fact: vLLM forwarded client-provided mm_processor_kwargs into multimodal image/video processor constructors, allowing resource-sensitive values to force out-of-memory termination. A separate defect trusted client-provided multimodal UUIDs as cache identities while unsynchronized frontend/engine caches could substitute incompatible stale tensors, allowing an unauthenticated client to kill the engine.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Unvalidated processor kwargs: vllm >=0.7.3 and <0.31.0. Forged UUID cache collision: vllm <0.31.0. Both affect remote multimodal request input to shared model-serving runtime availability; API authentication is optional.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade to vLLM 0.31.0. Reject non-empty per-request mm_processor_kwargs by default, bind cache identity to content, validate receiver-cache hits against request layout, and apply authentication, request limits, and resource isolation.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model-serving APIs must treat multimodal request metadata as hostile: unbounded preprocessing and cache identity drift can take down a shared inference service.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad vLLM and model-serving catalog context; this repository retains multimodal input validation, cache integrity, and availability controls.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for publication timing, fixed version, and both independently described crash paths. Preserve separate CVE boundaries during ingest despite their common 0.31.0 remediation.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, verify the 0.31.0 release packaging and write separate controls for processor-argument admission and cache-key integrity.
